newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ sees higher annual profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ sees higher annual profit.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to achieve higher earnings in the current financial year.

The bank, which earlier reported a six percent rise in 1995/96 (October/September) net profit to A$1.12 billion, also said it believed costs would be flat in the first half of 1996/97 and be reduced in the second half.

When asked by reporters if he expected growth in the bank's bottom line in 1996/97, chief executive Don Mercer replied: "That's certainly what a lot of people are expecting. We expect it of ourselves."
Mercer also predicted costs would decline in the later part of fiscal 1996/97.
"Our costs are going to be flat in the first half of next year and they will be coming down in the second half," he said.
Mercer said the bank expected asset growth to be reasonable in the current year, with the majority of the growth coming from international operations.

He refused to put a figure on expected job losses within the bank which form part of an on-going cost drive, but told reporters negotiations with the Finance Sector Union were "going better than you think".
Chief financial officer David Craig said the company's effective tax rate in fiscal 1996/97 was expected to be between 32 percent and 33 percent.
